scope: MINI-1906R complex import; local synthetic MySQL only
method: One independent sample per size/scenario; no P95 claim. Same-user and other-user manual writes start when the import acquires its user lock; no injected delay.
Parse/ingest and fixture construction are outside measured organizing command timings.
Combo/repayment use one public issue confirmation, then locally seed the same confirmed split; this is not full click-through performance.
Action heap before/after is not peak memory. Process max RSS is lifetime high-water including parse/ingest.
Rows=24990 uses five files of 4998 transactions; history copy uses a UTF-8 BOM to change bytes without extra CSV records.

Final evidence uses bounded validation cohorts: first four scenarios predate history-index/link batching, upgrade-mapping batching and confirmed-account set de-duplication; business output is unchanged. The final ordinary matrix exercises the common repository path.
History excludes repeated source identities before posting: lookup matches are reported separately from actual reused/created transaction counts.
failedTrials: Upper refund-pair prepare 26.368 s: issue member de-duplication/relation scan; set and per-event relation index.
Upper combo refresh 156.036 s query: optimizer used uid-only primary scan; use the existing issue-member index and update scope.
256 MiB heap failures: persistPlan and saveEvents serialized entire event arrays; now serialize only the current SQL chunk.
History synthetic copy appended blank records and exceeded the fixed CSV record limit; replace fixture bytes with a UTF-8 BOM. Product limit is unchanged.
Upper history prepare 85.139 s / 51011 SQL: existing identity/evidence indexes plus chunked version reads and historical links.
Upper upgrade 24.291 s / 26264 SQL: restore mappings with bounded inserts.

Upgrade remained 21.350 s after SQL batching; an action-only CPU profile located 5.340 s in confirmed-account member de-duplication. Set membership preserves order and reduces the 1000-row counter from 1000002 reads to <=5000.
